title: Context continuity recovery checklist and stress harness
content:
Status: working draft - this is the applied-ml canonical checklist and lightweight harness for detecting and recovering from context continuity failures during onboarding and regression runs.

High level goal:
- Define reproducible stress scenarios for 8k, 32k, and 128k retrieval+prompt shuffles and capture both graceful truncation and attention sink failure modes.
- Provide a small, automatable checklist teams can run locally and in CI to detect regressions when model variants or runtime optimizations are introduced.

Motivation / problem statement:
- We've seen occasional failures where retrieval-augmented prompts cause the model to ignore trailing context (attention sink) or generate plausible but hallucinated continuations after prefix truncation. These bugs crop up across quantized variant rollouts and routing fallbacks.
- Need a compact set of tests and signal definitions that are easy to run in the PR pipeline and that map to actionable mitigations (prefix culling, kv-cache refresh, retrieval sharding).

Definitions and new metrics (why new):
- Context Continuity Score (CCS): lightweight heuristic combining token-level agreement on retrieval anchors and relative similarity between top-k next-token distributions before/after truncation. Range 0-100. Lower values indicate continuity loss.
- Attention Sink Index (ASI): fraction of attention mass consumed by first N tokens of the sequence over long contexts. High persistent ASI (>0.6) correlated with dropped long-term retrieval signals.
- Truncation Break Rate (TBR): percent of prompts where final expected retrieval item is missing from generated output when the input is truncated by the runtime (simulates failure to include tail context).

Test harness overview (runnable locally or in CI):
- Harness repo: scripts/eval/context_harness/ (see linked PR)
- Steps:
  1) Build allocation with model variant (float16/4-bit/kv-compressed) and runtime flags (continuous-batching on/off, kv-compression on/off).
  2) Load standard prompt sets (see prompt set section) and associated retrieval stacks (dense vector store snapshots for 8k, 32k, 128k).
  3) Run each prompt with retrieval enabled and capture token-level logits, attention maps (when available), final completion, and runtime truncation logs.
  4) Compute CCS, ASI, TBR and latency percentiles.
  5) Compare to baseline commit for regression thresholds.

Prompt sets and construction notes (do not duplicate existing sets):
- continuity-case-anchors: 40 prompts designed around 3 anchor facts spaced across 8k/32k/128k. Anchor facts are short, unique strings (safe tokens) to make detection deterministic.
- jittered-retrieval-chains: 30 prompts where retrieval order is shuffled and overlapping context is introduced to test stable chaining.
- truncation-probe-recipes: 25 long synthetic prompts that deliberately place the important retrieval item near the end of the allowed context window to exercise runtime truncation behavior.
- soft-fallthrough-checks: 20 prompts where retrieval results conflict with the immediate prompt; verifies model prefers relevant retrieval info over spurious prefix.

Example prompt (continuity-case-anchor):
- system: you are a precise assistant. do not invent facts.
- user: here is the project history. [retrieved chunk A] ... [retrieved chunk B] ... [retrieved chunk C]. Who is listed as the release owner for feature Z? (anchor token: RELEASE_OWNER=maiden-name-237)

Stress scenarios (what to run):
- Level 1 (8k baseline): run continuity-case-anchors with 8k retrieval set. Expected CCS > 78, TBR < 3%, ASI < 0.45.
- Level 2 (32k stress): same prompts but with 32k retrieval set and intentionally increased retrieval noise (inject spurious docs at 10% rate). Expected CCS > 72, TBR < 5%. Note if ASI spikes after quantization.
- Level 3 (128k extreme): long-chaining prompts, simulated heavy prefix churn, forced kv-cache regeneration every 512 tokens. Expected CCS > 65. Flag runs where model output references a retrieval anchor not present in the provided docs.

Attention sink checks and probes (novel tests):
- rolling-prefix-dampen: incrementally prepend 500-token unrelated buffer to the front of a known-working prompt and measure how ASI and CCS change. Looks for monotonic degradation.
- anchor-redistribution: move anchor tokens from positions around token 2k -> 50k in 5 steps and assert continuity monotonicity.
- kv-fragmentation-scan: artificially split retrieval chunks into smaller fragments and measure whether the runtime recombines context or loses anchor binding.

Data collected per-run (minimum):
- raw completion text (string)
- token-level logits (downloadable artifact id)
- runtime truncation flag and truncated-nTokens
- attention mass summary per layer (if runtime exposes; otherwise approximate via gradient-proxy)
- latency: p50/p95/p99 (in ms) and tokens/sec
- CCS, ASI, TBR values

Regression detection rules (CI friendly):
- Hard fail if TBR increases by > 2 percentage points compared to baseline and absolute TBR > 5% for any level.
- Soft alert if CCS drops by 6 points or ASI increases by 0.12. Attach diffs and failure seeds to the PR.
- Require human triage for any run where model references nonexistent retrieval anchors.

Quick mitigation playbook (when failures observed):
- Re-run with kv-cache invalidation on request boundary. If continuity improves, file work item to add explicit kv refresh on retrieval mismatch.
- Reduce batching window or enable strict prefix-preservation mode for the failing route.
- Try alternative model variant (14B float16 vs 4-bit quant) to determine whether quantization is introducing attention collapse.
- If truncation is root cause, modify retrieval ranking to bias anchor items earlier in combined prompt or use chunked summarization to compress retrieval payload.

Automation and CI integration notes:
- Lightweight CI job should run Level 1 nightly against baseline and PR candidate for any changes touching runtime or model packaging.
- Full matrix (8k/32k/128k x variant) runs are expensive; include cost gating and run on merge-to-main for release candidates.
- Harness outputs artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/context-continuity/<run-id> with a JSON summary for quick triage.

Initial observations from exploratory runs (summary - empirical):
- Float16 baseline: stable CCS ~82 on Level 1, ASI ~0.38.
- 4-bit quantized variant: CCS dropped about 6-9 points on 32k runs with retrieval noise injected; ASI increased by ~0.1. Suggests attention redistribution under quantization.
- Runtime continuous-batching spike: p95 latency decreased, but ASI increased in some heavy-churn traces. Possible batching artifact where prefix gets higher attention due to kernel fusion.

Open tickets and next steps:
- JIRA-ML-2104: add CCS/ASI calculators to the eval harness and wire to PR checks. (owner: Liam)
- JIRA-ML-2187: expand prompt set coverage and add soft-fallthrough-checks to onboarding checklist. (owner: Zoe)
- Follow-up experiment: evaluate effect of prefix compression (RL-based summarizer) vs retrieval ranking adjustments on CCS. (owner: Marcus)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally includes some shorthand and embedded todo flags. The goal is to let applied-ml and serving-runtime teams iterate quickly. Please add comments inline in the PR or Slack thread.

Immediate todo before merging to canonical folder:
- commit harness README with run commands and small sample artifacts (small-run seed)
- attach baseline artifact ids for current main branch
- add a minimal plotting script that produces CCS/ASI time series png for triage

Sign-off checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] baseline artifacts uploaded and linked
- [ ] basic CI job green on Level 1 nightly
- [ ] owners assigned for open JIRA items

End of doc.
